doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: Teenage record collection and Charlie Parker
summary: His records at 15-16 were Bud Powell, Parker, Blakey, Mulligan, Baker and Art Tatum, and he praises Parker as a genius.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What was your record collection like when you were — oh I don’t know, 15 or 16?

Bud Powell, Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Charlie Parker, Art Blakey, Gerry Mulligan, Chet Baker, Art Tatum was a huge — I just listened to Art Tatum all the time. And all those guys. And then a few years later Billie Holiday came in the thing and I still listen to music — when I find something I need I listen to it obsessively. Mostly I don’t listen to music at all anymore but that’s — the record with Bud Powell and Bird and Jazz at Massey Hall — even though it’s a big mess, Charlie Parker’s — Jesus — Charlie Parker, the greatest, the greatest, the greatest. Genius like, and almost everybody else is building on somebody else but Charlie Parker was, Holy my God, sprung forth from what is it, sprung forth from Jupiter’s brow.
